## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Juṇhajātaka* (Ja 456) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral; Narada 2008]. Its framing narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana in Sāvatthī, delivered by the Buddha regarding the eight boons requested by Venerable Ānanda upon being selected as the Buddha's permanent attendant [SuttaCentral; Narada 2008; Fausböll 1887]. The opening verse of the text begins with the words *Suṇohi mayhaṁ vacanaṁ janinda* ("Listen to my words, O king of men") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1887].
In the story of the past (*atītavatthu*), the Bodhisatta was Prince Juṇha of Benares, who lived as a day-scholar studying at the educational center of Takkasīlā (Taxila) [Law 1931]. Leaving his teacher's house in the darkness of night, he accidentally collided with a brāhman and broke the brāhman's alms bowl [Law 1931]. Unable to pay compensation at the time because he resided there stripped of personal wealth, the prince gave his name and promised to reward the brāhman upon ascending the throne of Kāśī [Law 1931]. When Juṇha subsequently became king, the brāhman reminded him of the encounter, and the king fulfilled his pledge by bestowing great honor and wealth upon him [Law 1931; Fausböll 1887]. In the identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha explains that the brāhman of that past life was Ānanda, while King Juṇha was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1887].
Text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus shows extensive Pali-internal sharing with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Catuttho bhāgo, 14 matching segments covering §2.4–13.1) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments automatically with Tibetan works, notably the *Karmaśataka* (D0340-2) and the *Mahāyānasūtra* D0099 [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].
